title: Base
warrantyPowertrain: 3yr/unlimited mi (extendable via Power program up to 7yr)
warrantyBattery: 8yr/unlimited mi (hybrid components, per EU/US norms for PHEV battery)
infotainment: Ferrari proprietary touchscreen + digital instrument cluster + passenger display
adasStandard: Adaptive cruise, lane departure warning, automatic emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, traffic sign recognition, driver-attention monitoring (drowsiness). Sources: https://www.cars.com/research/ferrari-296_gtb-2025/
adasOptional: Driver Assistance Pack adds full ACC stop-and-go integration plus additional sensor suite refinements. Sources: https://www.cars.com/research/ferrari-296_gtb-2025/
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard rear-view camera with dynamic guidelines; resolution and multi-angle capability not specifically disclosed in Ferrari literature. Sources: https://www.continentalautosports.com/2025-ferrari-296-gtb-trim-levels/
sideViewCameraNotes: Data unavailable: Ferrari does not publish a surround-view (360) camera spec for the base 296 GTB in US-market documentation; surround-view appears in the Assetto Fiorano upgrade documentation but not as standard. No Honda-LaneWatch-style side-blind camera.
subscriptionFeatures: MyFerrari Connect services included in the purchase price; no separate subscription tier publicly disclosed. Apple CarPlay/Android Auto wireless integration included. No documented heated-seat or performance-feature subscription gating. Sources: https://www.ferrari.com/en-EN/auto/myferrari-connect
drmNotes: MyFerrari Connect telematics module is fitted as standard and continuously transmits chassis number, mileage, speed, battery state, charging timelines, software version, infotainment data, work history, scheduled maintenance, fuel level, tire pressure, emissions, and energy consumption to Ferrari and the owner's dealer. A Privacy Mode toggle in the MyFerrari app suspends data and GPS but does not disable the hardware. No documented case of Ferrari remotely disabling features post-sale. OTA updates handled through dealer service. Sources: https://www.ferrari.com/en-EN/auto/myferrari-connect
killSwitchNotes: Data unavailable: Ferrari has not deployed an impaired-driver kill switch and has not publicly disclosed its IIJA Section 24220 compliance plan as of May 2026. Driver-attention/drowsiness monitoring hardware is present but not gating drive authorization.
knownIssues: Reported infotainment screen lag and false dashboard warning lights on early 296 production cars; key-fob intermittent recognition issues. Sources: https://www.icartea.com/en/wiki/ferrari-reliability-what-owners-need-to-know-in-2025
recalls: Data unavailable: no major US NHTSA recall affecting 2025 296 GTB documented in publicly searchable databases as of May 2026. Sources: https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls
stateIncentives: Data unavailable: no broad US state PHEV incentive applies above the typical ~$80k MSRP cap; California CVRP excludes vehicles above $60k base MSRP. Sources: https://cleanvehiclerebate.org/
